messages:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: feature/rate-limiter-v2 -> us-west-2 (canary=5%). image=rl-inference:release-2026-03-15

sarah: seeing 429 spike from the canary pool, dashboards jumping. cc @matt on-call?

matt: on it. getting paged by PD. link to grafana: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/CRIT-1234

incident-bot: @matt, you were paged (pagerduty incident PD-7852) — high 429 error rate for api.generate tokens.

matt: joining call in 2. grabbing logs now.

julia: reported from SRE slack — multiple customers hitting elevated throttles, example from enterprise-corp: 5000 requests -> 429.

luis: quick snapshot from nginxs: 
```
[2026-05-31T12:12:05Z] "POST /v1/generate" 429 0ms - rate_limit_exceeded
[2026-05-31T12:12:06Z] "POST /v1/embeddings" 429 0ms - quota_reached
```

matt: can anyone confirm if exemptions on reserved routes were applied? those should bypass per-user burst.

sarah: checking repo: the deploy included change to token-accounting: https://git.redwood/rl/inference/commit/9f3a2c - looks like an ordering change.

julia: stack traces show rate limiter saw per-key token bucket with capacity=0 for some requests. seems like a conversion bug when the flag for "use-legacy-buckets" was toggled.

matt: immediate mitigation options: 1) kill canary via feature flag 2) rollback release 3) patch and hotfix. What's impact if we kill the flag?

luis: kill-switch should stop new requests using v2 limiter, existing canary pods will still run for a bit. killside effect: it flips on the old limiter which has exemptions intact.

ops-bot: runbook step: to flip feature flag: `curl -XPOST https://flags.redwood/api/feature/toggle -d '{"flag":"rate-limiter-v2","state":"off"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****'`

matt: executing kill-switch now.

sarah: confirmed flag toggled. HTTP return 200.

deploy-bot: Canary traffic routed back to v1 limiter. Monitoring for 2m.

julia: after kill-switch, 429 rate drops ~85% in the next 90s. dashboards show request success rate recovering.

matt: good. paging to PD is resolved; marking incident "mitigated" for customer-facing impact. keeping thread open for RCA.

sarah: quick customer-impact summary: estimated 3% global error increase during 12:11-12:18 UTC; ~12 customers reported elevated throttles (not full outage). highest impact: enterprise-corp had ~15% of API calls throttled. Support tickets created: TKT-8934, TKT-8935.

julia: root cause notes so far: rate-limiter v2 introduced a token-accounting change that assumed a per-tenant header `X-Tenant-Tokens` would be present. Canary traffic from dedicated clients did not include header, resulting in zero tokens and immediate throttles. test suites didn't catch it because integration harness always set header.

luis: reproduction repro steps: 
```
# simulate client without header
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -XPOST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' >/dev/null &
done
# observe 429s when v2 limiter active
```

matt: next actions: 1) rollback v2 from canary and stop rollout (done via kill-switch) 2) open critical PR to make header optional/fallback to per-tenant default token bucket 3) add integration test for missing-header path 4) notify affected customers + support playbook

sarah: PR opened: https://git.redwood/rl/inference/pull/7123 — patch includes fallback and additional logging. requesting hotfix review.

julia: also adding a quota-config validation to deployment pipeline to catch migrations that change account defaults without feature gating.

matt: for transparency — this was a release/regression, not a capacity issue. autoscaling behaved fine. the bad rollout changed token accounting logic.

ops-bot: Documentation updated: https://docs.redwood/platform/rate-limiter#migration-notes - added a checklist for feature-flagged rollouts w/ token schema changes.

luis: logistics: rolling back fully from canary to block rollout in other regions until fixed. deploy-bot: hold global rollout.

deploy-bot: Global rollout paused. Labeling release as blocked.

sarah: follow-up items assigned in the incident board: RCA, tests, customer comms, comp review. Target: full postmortem in 48h.

matt: final customer comms draft (support): "We briefly activated a new rate-limiting implementation which incorrectly assumed a header from certain clients, causing over-throttling for a subset of requests between 12:11-12:18 UTC. We have reverted to the previous limiter and are deploying a fix. We're proactively reaching out to tenants with elevated errors."

julia: will attach timeline and artifacts to postmortem. thanks all for quick response. :thumbsup:

luis: any objections to closing PD incident now that mitigation complete?

matt: closing PD and marking incident as mitigated. keeping thread open for follow-ups and postmortem notes.

incident-bot: Incident PD-7852 marked RESOLVED by @matt.

sarah: one more: add a regression test that deploy pipeline runs a smoke test hitting exempted routes with and without headers. that would have caught this.

julia: agreed. adding to onboarding checklist for release engineers.

luis: PR merged to canary branch with test and fix, planning redeploy to canary after QA sign-off.

matt: thanks team. I'll be on the follow-up call at 16:00 UTC to go through RCA draft.

sarah: closing notes: operational impact minimal due to quick recovery, customer impact localized. postmortem owners: julia + luis.

ops-bot: Postmortem card created: https://board.redwood/incidents/PM-4541

julia: locking thread for now, will append PM when ready.
